issues.line: Ran walking and 500 Hz QP force-balance controllers on the estimate with 0 falls in 5 × 60 s walks, after tracing a 4° lean
issues.problem: Accurate only with the startup turn, and the sentence carries that condition only implicitly ('after ... a 4 s startup turn'). The walking (scripted-trot) controller had 0/5 falls on the estimate with or without the turn. The QP controller on the estimate fell 1 of 5 without the 4 s startup turn and had 0 of 5 with it. Make the QP condition explicit.
issues.source: quadruped-eskf/claims.json qp_estimate_falls: 'QP controller fed the estimate: 1 fall in 5 × 60 s walks (0 in 5 after a 4 s startup turn)'; closed_loop_falls: '0 falls over 5 × 60 s walks with the controller fed the estimate'; results/qp_compare.json headline/estimate falls = 1, turn_first/estimate falls = 0.
issues.fix: Ran walking and 500 Hz QP force-balance controllers on the estimate with 0 falls in 5 × 60 s walks (QP after a 4 s startup turn), after tracing a 4° lean to weak tilt observability and removing it with that turn.

issues.line: Reached 0.013 m/s velocity RMSE over a 60 s walk, 100× lower than IMU-only dead reckoning (1.38 m/s)
issues.problem: '100×' is a derived ratio that appears in no source. 1.38 / 0.0128 ≈ 108×, so it understates rather than overstates, but it isn't in claims.json published_strings and make claims would flag it. The other derived figures in this version check out: 46% = (0.169−0.091)/0.169, and 58% = 60/103.
issues.source: quadruped-eskf/claims.json: velocity_rmse 0.013 m/s (10-seed mean 0.0128), imu_only_rmse 1.38 m/s; published_strings has no ratio. README.md quotes '128× better' only for seed 0 (0.0108 m/s).
issues.fix: Reached 0.013 m/s velocity RMSE over a 60 s walk vs. 1.38 m/s for IMU-only dead reckoning, ...

issues.line: false starts to zero, in closed-loop simulation on real recorded EMG, pinned by 26 GoogleTest tests in CI.
issues.problem: The 'false starts to zero' figure (62/min to 0) comes from the offline envelope study, which uses 200 real contractions and synthetic artefact spikes at 1 per second. It isn't from the closed-loop simulation, and that study doesn't run in CI. In CI, one test (Latency.RealEmgOnsetToMotion) pins the latency numbers, and another only checks that a single spike is rejected. It is still simulation, so this isn't a hardware overclaim.
issues.source: firmware/README.md: 'an onset has to hold for 20 ms ... takes false starts from 62 a minute to zero, at one artefact per second'; 'analysis/latency_study.py compares designs on 200 real contractions ... false starts with motion artefacts'; 'The test Latency.RealEmgOnsetToMotion pins these numbers in CI'; sim/test_core.cpp Activation.ConfirmWindowRejectsASpike.
issues.fix: Cut EMG-to-motion latency 58% (103 ms to 43 ms) with a Bayesian EMG estimator in closed-loop simulation on real recorded EMG, pinned in CI (26 GoogleTest tests); its 20 ms onset confirm took simulated artefact false starts from 62/min to zero.

issues.line: Raised cross-day gesture decoding from 31% to 87% in emulation over 115 days of real EMG by leading a 5-engineer
issues.problem: 'by leading a 5-engineer team' makes team leadership read as a cause of the accuracy gain. The sources tie the gain to the v2 board design, which was Troy's own redesign. The master links the two only loosely ('Led ... and redesigned ..., raising ...').
issues.source: master: 'Led a 5-engineer team and redesigned the 4-channel EMG board in KiCad ..., raising day-to-day gesture decoding from 31% to 87% in emulated tests'; index.html: 'My v2 redesign is schematic-complete'; orthosis-emg-decoder/README.md attributes v1's loss to its unbuffered inputs and rectifier.
issues.fix: Led a 5-engineer team; redesigned the 4-channel EMG board in KiCad (INA333, right-leg drive, ISO7763 isolation), raising cross-day gesture decoding from 31% to 87% in emulation over 115 days of real EMG.
